newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Most Australians reckon they can read and write good-ABS.
newsitem.headline: Most Australians reckon they can read and write good-ABS.

text.p: Most Australians rate their literacy and numeracy skills as "good" to "excellent", the Australian Bureau of Statistics said on Thursday.
Eighty-six percent of people aged 15 to 74 rated their reading skills as excellent or good, according to results from the first large scale survey of English language literacy in Australia.
This compared with 80 percent for writing skills and 79 percent for basic mathematics, the Bureau said.
The survey, conducted in 1996, found that people's self rating of their skill level decreased as age increased, the Bureau said.
In particular, a higher proportion of people aged 55 and over rated their skills as moderate or poor.

The survey found that of 9.6 million workers, 90 percent rated their reading skills for the needs of their job as excellent or good and 86 percent rated their writing skills for the needs of their job the same way.
Unemployed people were twice as likely to report needing help with literacy than employed people, it said.
In September, the bureau will release another report, this time containing objective assessments of Australians' literacy and numeracy skill levels, it added.
